name: Tomato Leaf Bacterial Canker
symptoms: leaves: Older leaves develop brown, scorched margins that curl upward and inward Distinct border between brown and green tissue, often with a thin yellow line Systemic infections can cause leaf wilting and firing (browning and collapse) stems: Light streaks develop that darken and split forming shallow cankers Vascular tissue discolored yellow to tan, pith may become reddish-brown and mealy or hollow Branches may break off easily in advanced infections fruit: Raised, white blisters on green or red fruit (‘bird's eye’ spots), 1/16–1/8 inch (3–4 mm) in diameter Fruit near calyx may have brown seeds due to vascular invasion seedlings: Poor growth, temporary wilting, lower leaves yellow and shrivel Symptoms often appear at flowering or later
management: prevention: Use disease-free seeds and transplants; certified seeds recommended Soak seeds in 130°F water for 25 minutes to reduce contamination Steam or disinfect greenhouse flats, benches, and potting media Rotate crops out of tomatoes for at least one season cultural: Incorporate plant debris thoroughly at season end Control nightshade weeds that may harbor bacteria Avoid working in fields when foliage is wet Minimize overhead irrigation and handle plants carefully to reduce wounding chemical: Copper bactericides may reduce spread during wet conditions, but do not control systemic infections Disinfect tools and surfaces with 0.5–1% calcium or sodium hypochlorite, or commercial disinfectants like Physan
sources: Jones, J.B., et al. 2014. Compendium of Tomato Diseases and Pests, 2nd Edition. APS Press.
University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources. Tomato Pest Management Guidelines: Bacterial Canker.
Schaad, N.W., et al. 2001. Bacterial Cankers of Tomato. Plant Health Progress.
